map.none: inventory of flaky tests from repeated runs and gate logs is report work; no test checks it
classification of flake kinds with evidence is report work; no test checks it

tests.name: the workspace watcher > delivers a burst of writes as one batch, skips .git and node_modules, and keeps one watcher per folder
tests.why: rewritten to use injected watcher events and fake timers instead of OS events and fixed sleeps; guards batching behaviour the base already had

tests.name: the workspace watcher > drops an event the system delivers again for a file unchanged since its last batch, and still reports its next write
tests.why: same deterministic-trigger fix applied; behaviour unchanged from base

tests.name: the workspace watcher > hears a real write from the operating system
tests.why: new test keeps one real OS-event contract with a condition wait, since the others now inject events; behaviour existed at base

map.none: 30 loaded unit runs and 10 browser runs are evidence in the report; no test checks it

tests.name: test hygiene > adds no fixed sleep to a test: wait for a condition with until(), vi.waitFor, expect.poll or a web-first assertion
tests.why: the guard: fails when a test file gains a fixed sleep beyond its recorded count; title quotes the MUST's fixed-sleep-in-a-test wording

tests.name: test hygiene > uses no shared default port: browser tests take AMC_E2E_PORT and unit tests listen on port 0
tests.why: the port guard over test sources

tests.name: test hygiene > catches a new fixed sleep
tests.why: self-check that the sleep pattern matches two sleep forms; title quotes the MUST's new-fixed-sleep wording

map.none: docs/testing.md and report drafts are documentation; no test checks them

tests: tests/unit/watch.test.ts::the workspace watcher > hears a real write from the operating system
findings.note: test-focus finding: after nested-file checks switched to injected events, the only real OS-event test writes at the folder root, so a break in delivery for files in subfolders would go unseen; this is lost coverage of existing behaviour, not something a base-failing test would show

tests: tests/unit/test-hygiene.test.ts::test hygiene > adds no fixed sleep to a test: wait for a condition with until(), vi.waitFor, expect.poll or a web-first assertion
tests/unit/test-hygiene.test.ts::test hygiene > catches a new fixed sleep
findings.note: test-focus finding: the sleep pattern misses a common setTimeout-in-a-promise form and counts matches in comments or strings; the self-check covers only two forms, so the guard cannot fail on that regression

tests: tests/unit/test-hygiene.test.ts::test hygiene > uses no shared default port: browser tests take AMC_E2E_PORT and unit tests listen on port 0
findings.note: test-focus finding: the port guard scans only the tests folder, so the browser runner's config that still defaults to the shared port passes it

notes: Four of six MUSTs are process, evidence or documentation work with no test. Changed watcher tests import a test hook renamed in this branch, so on base they fail at import, not on an assertion; they guard existing behaviour and are marked PASS_TO_PASS. Review read from flake-3-review1.jsonl.
